newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-AN A-Z GUIDE TO A WET WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AN A-Z GUIDE TO A WET WIMBLEDON.

text.p: LONDON, June 26, Reuter - It's been a wet Wimbledon with no early respite in sight. Here is an A-Z guide to the soggy 1997 championships...

A is for Anna. The 16-year-old Russian Anna Kournikova has made a startling Wimbledon debut, on and off the court. When she sashayed into the All England Club this week, she attracted some whistles from a couple of admiring male spectators. "You could never afford me," Kournikova informed them icily.
B is for Brits. A laughing stock for years, but not for much longer if Greg Rusedski and Tim Henman continue to fly the flag when the courts dry out.

C is for Cliff. After last year's infamous Centre Court sing-song, no-one has yet dared thrust a microphone into the great entertainer's hands. Until it stops raining, though, no-one can relax totally.

D is for Dickie Bird. The English cricket umpire, famous for attracting rain wherever he goes. They should have known the inevitable would happen when he was offered a seat in the Royal Box on Thursday....
E is for Embarrassing. According to John McEnroe, the best description of the current state of men's tennis.
F is for Faithful Fans. More than 100,000 turned up on the first three days, a slight increase on the 1996 attendance, in spite of the abysmal weather.
G is for Grass. Assuming it is still there underneath all the tarpaulins.

H is for Horse-riding. World number one Martina Hingis is preparing to get back on a horse at a local stables on Sunday, despite having only recently recovered from a knee injury suffered in a fall in April.

I is for the Internet. Wimbledon have established their own web site for the first time this year, little guessing the All England Club would be able to offer facilities to the sort of surfers who don't use computer terminals.
J is for Jamaica. Where disillusioned hacks reckon Centre Court should be relocated before next year.
K is for Knickers. Previously the only place where sponsor's logos never strayed, until now. Monica Seles has permitted Nike to open up a whole new ball-game.
L is for Long-range forecasts. The outlook is distinctly gloomy for the rest of the week.
M is for Mills. The long-suffering Wimbledon referee Alan Mills, increasingly resigned to the prospect of another day's work on Monday week.
N is for Noah. Boris Becker's three-year-old son, as well as the ultimate expert in wet weather conditions.
O is for Oakley. British journalist John Oakley has seen it all before. This is his 52nd consecutive Wimbledon, making him the longest-serving journalist at the championships.

P is for Puns. Beloved of feature writers praying for the day they can cover Draper playing Kuerten in the men's singles, or the mouth-watering women's showdown between Grande and Brandi. Q is for Queues. Still stretching around the block, despite the weather. Britain's reputation as a nation of eccentrics is safe for another year.
R is for Results. So far only 94 singles matches have been completed, with a backlog of around 130 matches.

S is for Strawberries. Always popular, particularly when handed out to hungry reporters in the press restaurant on Thursday by Mary Pierce and Mary Joe Fernandez. They were instantly voted the best servers of the tournament.
T is for Tarango. Already gone, but not forgotten by the ball-girl accused by the American charmer of acting 'like the Statue of Liberty'.

U is for Unlucky. The female spectator who queued up all night in the rain on the pavement outside the All England Club, only to slip and suffer a broken leg when she finally made it into the grounds.
V is for Venus. Miss Williams has not been sighted on court yet but is set to make a dazzling impression in the women's singles, if only because of her specially-chosen purple-and-green hair beads.
W is for Wash-out. These are shaping up to be the wettest championships since 1991 when only nine hours 15 minutes of play were possible in the first week.
X is for X-Files. Or any other television programme which keeps boredom at bay for an hour or two.
Y is for Yachting. What they'll be staging on Centre Court unless it stops raining soon.
Z is for Zilch. The chances of the sun reappearing this week.
